memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said to Moses, 'Tell the Israelites to bring me an offering. You are to receive the offering for me from everyone whose heart prompts them to give.'" - Exodus 25:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins the tabernacle project not with blueprints but with hearts. He asks for an offering, but notice the condition: from everyone whose heart prompts them to give. No quotas, no compulsion, no shaming. God wanted willing gifts from glad hearts, not reluctant contributions squeezed out of duty.

This tells us something beautiful about our God. He owns everything already; He does not need our money or materials. What He desires is our hearts, and giving is simply one honest window into where our hearts truly are. A gift given grudgingly says one thing; a gift given gladly says another. God looks past the amount to the willingness behind it.

Paul echoes this exactly: each person should give what they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7). Generosity in God's kingdom is never extracted; it is inspired. When we grasp how freely God has given to us — His own Son, no less — our hands naturally open. If your giving has become a grim obligation, the answer is not to try harder but to look again at His generosity toward you. Willing hearts follow grateful ones.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is my giving prompted by a willing heart or by reluctant obligation?
How does remembering God's generosity toward me change my own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You gave me Your very best without being forced. Free my heart from grudging duty and make me a glad and willing giver, generous because You have been generous to me. Amen.
